page: Microsoft Azure E32s_v6 is a memory-optimized instance operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor. The system provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a sizable 260 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is fixed at 256 GB, offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent processing performance, with PassMark CPU scoring 46370.85 and Geekbench reaching 15353.0 in multi-core evaluation. Supported by Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instructions, the server handles vector-heavy tasks capably, registering strong results in image processing (14000.0) and small-model LLM text generation (390.88 tokens/sec). Network and memory bandwidth tests show sustained web serving throughput of 54.65 GB/sec, alongside large-block uncached read speeds of 146.81 GB/sec and write speeds of 62.39 GB/sec.

A primary operational tradeoff is the complete absence of local temporary or ephemeral storage, requiring workloads to rely exclusively on remote attached volumes such as Premium Storage. While PassMark memory synthetic scores rate in the lower quartile, raw cached small-block read speeds reach 2173.18 GB/sec. This configuration offers high memory density relative to core count, making the instance well structured for in-memory databases like Redis, distributed caching layers, data processing pipelines, and enterprise application backends requiring high memory overhead without dedicated GPU resources.
description: Microsoft Azure E32s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz. Designed for memory-intensive environments, it provides 256 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, complemented by 260 MB of L3 cache and support for AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. Local storage is not included, requiring external premium disk attachments for file persistence, and no hardware GPU accelerators are present. Benchmarks highlight solid execution in multi-threaded workflows, delivering 54.65 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 390.88 tokens/sec in lightweight LLM text generation. While synthetic memory benchmarks show lower relative efficiency under certain tests, its high memory-to-core ratio and robust vector compute capabilities make it suitable for large-scale caching, in-memory databases like Redis, and memory-constrained enterprise analytics.
